title: Boundary condition semantic model and format mapping
overview: Boundary conditions connect mesh patch identity, physical meaning, mathematical constraints, required state data and solver realization. Mesh owns geometric entities and patch identity; Boundary Conditions owns physical semantics and format/solver mapping; Parameter and Case own runtime values and scenario selection. The current Gmsh-to-CGNS alias map and CGNS-to-OneFLOW broad category map are summarized in the Boundary Model view.
principle: A boundary name is not a physical condition. Inlet is a patch identity; velocity inlet, mass-flow inlet and pressure inlet are distinct physical formulations with different prescribed and derived data. Wall does not specify slip/no-slip or thermal treatment. The mathematical condition must be stated independently of Gmsh and CGNS enum values. Missing state data must remain missing rather than being silently defaulted.
architecture: Mesh patch identity -> physical boundary semantic contract -> format adapter (Gmsh Physical Group / CGNS BC_t and BCType_t) -> OneFLOW broad BC category -> solver-specific numerical treatment and runtime state. Gmsh aliases: Inlet/Inflow/VelocityInlet/MassFlowInlet/PressureInlet -> BCInflow (9); Outlet/Outflow/PressureOutlet -> BCOutflow (13); Symmetry/SymmetryPlane -> BCSymmetryPlane (16); Farfield/Freestream -> BCFarfield (7); NoSlipWall/ViscousWall -> BCWallViscous (22); SlipWall/InviscidWall -> BCWallInviscid (21); Wall/LowerWall/UpperWall/BodyWall -> BCWall (20); unknown -> BCTypeUserDefined (1). CGNS-to-OneFLOW enum mapping (the names below are the BC class members declared in codes/geometry/include/Boundary.h): BCTypeNull -> BC::INTERFACE; BCTypeUserDefined -> BC::GENERIC_2; BCSymmetryPlane -> BC::SYMMETRY; inflow variants -> BC::INFLOW; outflow variants -> BC::OUTFLOW; wall variants -> BC::SOLID_SURFACE; BCDegenerateLine -> BC::POLE; BCFarfield -> BC::FARFIELD; BCGeneral -> BC::OVERSET. Unlisted CGNS types currently fall back to BC::GENERIC_2. These are broad category mappings only; they do not identify a complete physical formulation or prove solver-level numerical support.

proves: Boundary Conditions is registered as a separate Contract Workbench domain.
The architecture distinguishes mesh patch identity, physical semantics, format representation and solver realization.
The listed Gmsh aliases and current CGNS-to-OneFLOW broad categories are present in source.
does_not_prove: All physical boundary formulations are implemented by every OneFLOW solver.
Required state data are fully represented in current mesh conversion formats.
A mapped boundary type is sufficient to run or validate a CFD case.
